A tagged PDF now reads rich text where it stands, and what you ask of a rich text is done.

**Upgrade if you produce tagged PDFs, or use `AdvancedTextItem`, which is everything the content editor
writes.** This changes what those documents come out as: see "Worth checking" below. Documents with no rich
text come out as they did, to the byte. Nothing was removed or renamed in the public API, and the template
format has no new properties.

## Fixed: a tagged PDF read rich text out of order

The words of an `AdvancedTextItem` were written as paragraphs of their own at the root of the structure tree,
in every file since the first release:

- a rich table cell was an empty `TD`, and its words came after the table;
- a rich paragraph was read after every plain text on its page;
- each line and each change of style was a separate paragraph;
- a rich heading was no heading, and a language set on a rich text was lost.

A screen reader read those documents out of order, in files claiming PDF/UA-1. veraPDF passes such a file on
both profiles, because a well-formed tree in the wrong order is not something a profile tests, so a green
validator did not show this.

A rich text is now one element per page, holding its words in reading order, with the role and language it
was given. With no role it is a paragraph, or a cell in a table row.

## Fixed: what you asked of a rich text was not done

| Asked of an `AdvancedTextItem` | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `PageScope` in a header or footer, or on a group above it | ignored: a footer meant for the last page showed on every page | honoured |
| `Visibility.Invisible` | drawn | not drawn, and its room is kept |
| `Style.Background`, `Style.Border` | not drawn | drawn, under its words |
| `Bookmark` | not in the outline | in the outline, once, even if the text is split |
| `Style.RenderedFrame` | `NaN` | where it landed |
| `Style.Padding.Bottom`, in a stacked group | ignored: the next item sat on it | counted |

`fits.overflow` now names a rich text asked to stay whole and taller than a page, as it does a plain one.

## Worth checking

- **Every tagged PDF holding rich text changes**, though not on the page. If you compare files byte for byte,
  expect them to differ.
- **A rich text with a role now has that role**, so PDF/UA's rules apply to it. A document whose first heading
  is a rich `Heading2` was not refused while it was no heading, and is now: headings have to start at H1. A rich
  text with the `Figure` role owes an `AltText`. Run veraPDF over a tagged document once before shipping this.
- **Documents may change on the page** if a rich text carries any setting in the table above: words gone from
  pages their scope never included, a background appearing, items below a padded rich text moving down, and page
  breaks moving with them. Each is what the template always said.
